title: Dynamic High-Throughput Cell Death Screening of Primary Phagocytes
author: Skrabanja, Klazen, et al.
materials: Black/clear polystyrene flat bottom imaging 96-well plate

Timing: 15–30 min setup of analysis masks
Timing: 3–4 h analysis run time

Masking of the cell death markers is an important step in the high-throughput screening analysis (Graphical abstract, step 4). Here in steps 22–31, the protocol describes how to correctly mask for the fluorescent signal of the area in the Incucyte S3 software and export it to a text file.CRITICAL: If one condition or a whole experiment needs drastically different analysis settings than other experiments, you can consider excluding it.CRITICAL: We recommend keeping the threshold values for masking similar between experiments as this helps for objective analysis. However, one should always consider if the masking threshold is correctly applied.Note: Setting the perfect mask will be difficult to achieve, so go for the best fit that suits all conditions in one experiment.Note: Setting the mask is partially subjective, since the Incucyte Software shows a suggestion that you can fine-tune by increasing or decreasing the threshold values.22.To set the mask, open your experiment in the Incucyte Software and go to ‘View’.a.Press ‘Launch Analysis’.b.In the pop-up tab ‘No Spectral’, select ‘Yes’ to go the next tab.c.In the next tab ‘New or Use Existing Analysis Definition’ press ‘+ Create New Analysis Definition’.d.Press ‘Next’ to go to the new tab for analysis.e.In the tab ‘Analysis Type’, select ‘Basic Analyzer’ and proceed to ‘Next’ to go to next tab.f.In the tab ‘Image Channels’, select the channels you want to analyze.g.Press ‘Next’ to go to the ‘Image Set Selection’ tab.23.In the tab ‘Image Set Selection’ you go to a representative time point that shows both positive and negative cells, for example a 24-h time point.a.In the overview of the 96-wells plate you select representative images/wells of each condition to base your masking on.b.When finished, press ‘next’ to go to the new ‘Analysis Definition’ tab.Note: You can select as many representative images as possible. With more images it will take more time to check the masking on all of them, but it will be more representative. One of each condition at the 24-h time point is usually sufficient.24.In the tab ‘Analysis Definition’ under ‘Green Channel’ tab, adjust the Threshold (GCU) based on every selected image to make sure that the mask is optimal for all conditions.Note: We consider the mask optimal when as little background as possible is taken along for the masking and that also the masking truly reflects the cell death signal in the field of view. See Figure 7 for correct and incorrect masking with over or under estimation of the signal and their settings.a.Press ‘Preview Current’ to check if the mask is correctly applied for the green channel (AnnexinV-FITC in this protocol) and change if this needs adjustment.Note: In the experimental set up of this protocol, we changed the Threshold (GCU) from 2.000 (default) to 0.4000. This depends on the background per imaging plate and per experiment and conditions but should be similar.b.Make sure the masking area is the same within one experiment and has similar results between different experiments with same conditions.CRITICAL: You have to critically assess the threshold settings for each experiment, and you are allowed to adjust the threshold settings of the green and red channel. However, you can also adjust the threshold by adjusting Segmentation, Edge split on or off, Clean up or Filters. If you use these settings, do this also for the next experiments.CRITICAL: It is essential that the masking of background is minimized so that the mask truly reflects cell death signal in the field of view.25.Repeat the previous step for the ‘Red Channel’ (SytoxAADvanced in this protocol) tab.a.After the mask is set, press ‘Next’ to go to the next ‘Scan Time and Wells’ tab.26.In the tab ‘Scan Time and Wells’, select all the wells and time points you want to include in your analysis.Note: In the high-throughput screening assay of this protocol, we included all time points up to 5 days including the time points after addition of 0.5% Triton X-100 to make sure that we reached the maximum value to do the normalization.a.Press ‘Next’ to go to the next ‘Save and apply Analysis Definition’ tab.27.In the tab ‘Save and apply Analysis Definition’, give the analysis a name.a.Press ‘Next’ to go to the last ‘Summary’ tab.28.In the ‘Summary’ tab, check the settings before launching the analysis.a.Press ‘Next’ when everything is set correctly.b.The analysis will now run.Note: The time for the analysis to run depends on the number of conditions, channels and time intervals. The screening described in this protocol takes 3–4 h.29.When the analysis has completed, you export the data by clicking on ‘Graph Metrics’.a.Select under the Green or Red subtab ‘Total Area (μm2/Image)’.b.Select all time points up to the moment that the maximal value is reached (this might be a couple of hours after addition of 0.5% Triton X-100).c.Select all the wells that you want to export.Note: In this protocol, we select ‘Plate Map Replicates’ in Select Grouping, to make sure that all conditions have the name that you assigned to each condition during setting up of the Plate Map.d.Press ‘Export Data’.e.In the tab ‘Graphing Export’, select where you want to save your file and check the box ‘Include Experiment details in header’.f.Press ‘Export’ to export the file as text file in the selected folder.g.The data of the green and red channel are exported as separate text files.Optional: You can also export the data to ‘clipboard’ and paste directly in a text or excel file.Note: Here, we export the data via the ‘Export Data’ because we want to directly have the data in a text file to manually change the decimal ‘.’ to ‘,’. You can also change to copy it to clipboard into Excel, but then you must change the R script for normalization.Note: In this protocol, each experiment consists of conditions of two technical replicates with three images each per well (so six images per condition per experiment). The protocol describes exporting the outcome of the mean total area of one condition in one experiment, based on the mean of six images by the Incucyte Analysis Software.Optional: You can change this by exporting the data of each well separately.30.To do this, ‘Select Grouping’.31.Select ‘None’ and export data under ‘Layout’ as: ‘Row by Row A1, A2, A3, … B1, B2, B3, …’ and under ‘Other Options’: ‘Break Data down in individual images’.Note: This protocol uses the Total Area (μm2/Image) instead of the object count since clusters of death cells may be quantified as one object while it consists of multiple death cells. Therefore, we recommend Total Area as better measurement for quantifying total cell death compared to cell count.Figure 7Overview of the manual masking in the Incucyte S3 Analysis Software(A and B) Masking for AnnexinV-FITC signal (Green Channel) for well E1 (PS 1 μm 100 μg/mL condition) for time point 24 h. The different masking is visualized a check under Green Object (lining in Red). Under masking of the AnnexinV with threshold at 2.000 (default) (A), over masking with threshold at 0.1000 (B) and correct masking with threshold at 0.4000 (C).

steps.title: Prepare ACK lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Make ammonium‑chloride‑potassium (ACK) lysis buffer (155 mM NH4Cl, 10 mM KHCO3, 0.1 mM Na2EDTA, phenol red) in 0.5 L autoclaved glass bottle, filter and store.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.4 L Milli‑Q water to an autoclaved 0.5 L glass bottle.
Weigh 4.15 g NH4Cl, 0.5 g KHCO3, 18.6 mg Na2EDTA, 0.2 g phenol red and add to the water; mix by inversion.
Add 0.1 L Milli‑Q water to bring volume to 0.5 L; stir at 4 °C for 15 min, ensuring complete dissolution.
Adjust pH to 7.4 at 4 °C (equivalent to pH 6.9 at 20 °C) with 1.25 M NaOH or 37 % HCl as needed.
Measure osmolarity (295–309 mOsm) with an osmometer; adjust with water or buffer if outside range.
Sterilize by 0.22 µm Steritop filtration in a BSL‑1 cabinet (disinfect bottle exteriors with 70 % EtOH, use vacuum suction).
Store at 4 °C up to 6 months; discard if phenol red turns yellow/orange (pH drop).

steps.title: Prepare PBS2+ wash buffer
steps.instruction: Make PBS2+ (PBS + 4 g L⁻¹ Albuman + 0.32 % w/v trisodium citrate) and aliquot for later use.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 3.2 % w/v TSC: mix 10.67 mL 30 % TSC with 89.33 mL Milli‑Q water (final 100 mL).
In a 0.5 L autoclaved bottle combine 800 mL PBS, 100 mL 3.2 % TSC, and 100 mL Albuman (40 g L⁻¹). Mix by inversion.
Aliquot 40 mL portions into 50 mL sterile tubes; store at –20 °C ≤ 1 year or at 4 °C ≤ 1 week.
Maintain sterility throughout preparation.

steps.title: Prepare HEPES3+ culture buffer
steps.instruction: Make HEPES buffer (20 mM HEPES, 132 mM NaCl, 6 mM KCl, 1 mM MgSO4·7H2O, 1.2 mM KH2PO4), adjust pH, filter, aliquot, then supplement with glucose, CaCl2 and Albuman.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 L Milli‑Q water to an autoclaved 1 L glass bottle.
Weigh and add: 4.77 g HEPES, 7.71 g NaCl, 0.45 g KCl, 0.25 g MgSO4·7H2O, 0.16 g KH2PO4; invert to mix.
Adjust pH to 7.4 at 21 °C with 1.25 M NaOH or 37 % HCl.
Measure osmolarity; target 280 mOsm (adjust with water or buffer).
Sterilize by 0.22 µm filtration in a BSL‑1 cabinet; aliquot 40 mL into sterile tubes, store at –20 °C ≤ 1 year.
Just before use, thaw an aliquot and add:
80 µL sterile 2.5 M D‑(+)-glucose (final 100 mM).
400 µL sterile 100 mM CaCl2 (final 1 mM).
1 mL sterile Albuman 200 g L⁻¹ (final 5 g L⁻¹).
Mix gently; store at 4 °C ≤ 1 week (cannot be frozen after Albuman addition).

steps.title: Prepare supplemented RPMI medium
steps.instruction: Make RPMI 1640 with 2 mM L‑glutamine and add human pooled serum (HPS) for adherence and wash media.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 mL 200 mM L‑glutamine to 500 mL RPMI 1640 (final 2 mM).
For adherence medium: add 4 mL HPS to 36 mL of the above (10 % v/v).
For wash medium: add 0.4 mL HPS to 39.6 mL of the above (1 % v/v).
Store all preparations at 4 °C ≤ 3 months.
Do NOT use the 1 % or 10 % HPS RPMI for experimental conditions (to keep final HPS ≤ 10 %).

steps.title: Prepare 0.5% Triton X‑100 solution
steps.instruction: Make a 0.5 % (v/v) Triton X‑100 solution in PBS for maximal cell death after imaging.

substeps.instruction: Add 40 mL PBS to a sterile 50 mL tube.
Cut the tip of a 1 mL pipette tip.
Pipette 200 µL Triton X‑100 stock with the cut tip into the PBS.
Vortex thoroughly until fully dissolved (pre‑warm PBS to 37 °C if flakes form).
Store at 4 °C ≤ 3 months under sterile conditions.

steps.title: Dilute blood and layer over Ficoll
steps.instruction: Dilute whole blood 1:1 with PBS2+ and carefully layer onto Ficoll for density gradient separation.

substeps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, place two 50 mL tubes per donor.
Add 10 mL Ficoll‑Paque Plus to one tube.
Transfer the whole blood (e.g., 9 mL) from a sodium‑heparin tube into the empty 50 mL tube.
Add an equal volume of PBS2+ (e.g., 9 mL) to achieve a 1:1 dilution (total 18 mL).
Slowly layer the 18 mL blood/PBS2+ mixture onto the 10 mL Ficoll by pipetting against the tube wall, keeping the tube at a 30–45° angle to avoid mixing.
Centrifuge the tube at 845 × g for 20 min at 21 °C with acceleration 2 and deceleration 1.
Do not disturb the erythrocyte pellet after the run; keep all tubes at 4 °C thereafter.

steps.title: Isolate monocytes (PBMC layer)
steps.instruction: Collect PBMCs, wash, seed, and allow adherence before particle exposure.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 mL cold PBS2+ to a new 50 mL tube (keep on ice).
Using a Pasteur pipette, carefully aspirate the PBMC layer (between plasma and Ficoll) without taking excess plasma/Ficoll and transfer to the PBS2+ tube.
Centrifuge at 475 × g, 4 °C for 5 min; discard supernatant.
Wash again with 10 mL PBS2+ and repeat centrifugation (475 × g, 5 min, 4 °C).
Resuspend the pellet in RPMI + 2 mM L‑glutamine + 10 % HPS (prepared in step 4).
Count cells; seed 5 × 10⁵ total cells per well of a black/clear polystyrene 96‑well imaging plate (≈1 × 10⁵ monocytes per well, assuming ~20 % monocytes).
Incubate at 37 °C for 3 h to allow monocyte adherence.
After incubation, remove medium with a vacuum suction device, being careful to avoid drying cells.
Add 200 µL supplemented RPMI + 1 % HPS to each well (wash step).
Remove wash medium with a multichannel pipette, leaving adherent monocytes.

steps.title: Isolate neutrophils (granulocyte layer)
steps.instruction: Remove plasma/PBMCs, lyse erythrocytes with ACK buffer, wash, and resuspend neutrophils in HEPES3+.

substeps.instruction: If monocytes are not needed, discard the PBMC layer and plasma; otherwise, perform step 8 first.
Swab the inner wall of the 50 mL tube with a sterile cotton swab to remove residual sticky PBMCs.
Add 35 mL ACK‑lysis buffer (7:1 buffer:cell volume) to the erythrocyte‑granulocyte pellet.
Incubate on ice (4 °C) for 15 min, gently shaking at ~7 min.
Centrifuge 475 × g, 4 °C for 5 min; aspirate supernatant.
Add 25 mL fresh ACK‑lysis buffer, repeat centrifugation (475 × g, 5 min, 4 °C) and aspirate.
Wash cells with 10 mL PBS2+ (4 °C), centrifuge 475 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; aspirate.
Resuspend pellet in 500 µL HEPES3+; count granulocytes (e.g., Cell Dyn Emerald).
Adjust concentration to 17.5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ with HEPES3+; keep on ice (4 °C) and use within 2 h.
Acceptable purity ≥ 90 % (reject if < 85 %).

steps.title: Opsonize particles in human pooled serum
steps.instruction: Incubate each particle stock with HPS to promote phagocytosis.

substeps.instruction: For 0.20 µm PS (2.7 % w/v stock): add 7.4 µL stock to 192 µL HPS (1:27 dilution).
For 1 µm PS (10 % w/v stock): add 2 µL stock to 198 µL HPS (1:100).
For 10 µm PS (10 % w/v stock): add 2 µL stock to 198 µL HPS (1:100).
For 1 µm silica (5 % w/v stock): add 4 µL stock to 196 µL HPS (1:50).
For 10 µm silica (5 % w/v stock): add 4 µL stock to 196 µL HPS (1:50).
Incubate all mixtures 30 min at 21 °C.
(Optional) Heat‑inactivate HPS at 56 °C for 30 min if complement interference is a concern.

steps.title: Prepare monocyte compound mix
steps.instruction: Create 440 µL of reagent mix per duplicate for monocyte plating.

substeps.instruction: Label Eppendorf tubes for each condition.
Add 389.7 µL RPMI + 2 mM L‑glutamine (no HPS).
Add 4.4 µL 100 mM CaCl2 (gives 1 mM final).
Add 1.46 µL AnnexinV‑FITC (90 µg mL⁻¹ stock → 0.3 µg mL⁻¹ final).
Add 0.44 µL SytoxAA‑Advanced (1 mM stock → 1 µM final).
Add the appropriate volume of opsonized particle suspension (see step 9) to reach the desired particle concentration (0, 1, 10, 100 µg mL⁻¹).
Add sterile HPS to bring the total HPS concentration to 10 % v/v (adjust volume per condition as in Table 2).
Mix by pipetting up‑and‑down; keep on ice.
Just before adding to the plate, remove the 1 % HPS wash medium from the monocyte wells.
Add 200 µL of the compound mix to each well (duplicate wells per condition).

steps.title: Set up Incucyte S3 imaging
steps.instruction: Load the 96‑well plate, configure schedule, scan settings, and start acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Place the plate in the Incucyte holder without tilt; press ‘+’ in Schedule overview to create a new measurement.
Select ‘Scan on Schedule’, click ‘Next’.
Choose ‘Standard’ scan type; click ‘Next’.
In Scan Settings, leave Cell‑by‑Cell = ‘None’, check ‘Phase’, ‘Green’, and ‘Red’ channels.
Set objective to 20× magnification.
Proceed to Vessel Selection; choose the correct plate serial number.
In Vessel Selection tab, confirm plate type (Corning/Falcon 96‑well, Cat#353219).
In Channel Location, select the vessel drawer where the plate sits.
In Scan Pattern, select all wells and set ‘Images per well’ = 3.
In Vessel Notebook, create or import a plate map indicating condition names.
In Analysis Setup, keep default analysis type; click ‘Next’.
In Scan Schedule, set a start delay of ≥ 15 min after plate placement, then choose imaging interval (e.g., 1 h). Ensure total scan time per hour ≤ 30 min.
In Total Duration, select ‘Scan Indefinitely’ or set stop time (recommended 5 days).
Review Summary; press ‘Add to Schedule’ to start acquisition.
Monitor the first scan; verify focus and adjust if needed.

steps.title: Define analysis mask in Incucyte software
steps.instruction: Create a mask for AnnexinV‑FITC (green) and SytoxAA‑Advanced (red) to quantify total death‑cell area.

substeps.instruction: Open the experiment, go to ‘View’ → ‘Launch Analysis’.
Select ‘No Spectral’, click ‘Yes’, then ‘+ Create New Analysis Definition’.
Choose ‘Basic Analyzer’; click ‘Next’.
Select the imaging channels to analyze; click ‘Next’.
In Image Set Selection, pick a representative 24‑h time point and select one well per condition.
Proceed to Analysis Definition; for the Green channel set Threshold (GCU) to 0.4000 (adjust if needed).
Preview the mask; ensure minimal background and accurate representation of AnnexinV‑FITC signal.
Repeat for the Red channel (SytoxAA‑Advanced), adjusting threshold as required.
In Scan Time and Wells, select all wells and time points (including post‑Triton X‑100).
Save the analysis definition with a descriptive name; click ‘Next’ to Summary and launch the analysis.

After analysis completes (≈ 3–4 h), export data: choose ‘Total Area (µm²/Image)’ for each channel, select all time points up to maximal signal, include all wells, and click ‘Export Data’ to a text file (include experiment details).

steps.title: Normalize data with R script
steps.instruction: Convert Incucyte text files to normalized percentages using the provided R script.

substeps.instruction: Install the ‘xlsx’ package in RStudio (install.packages("xlsx", dependencies=TRUE)).
Set the working directory to the folder containing the exported text files (setwd("X:/..." )).
Read a text file, skipping the first 6 header rows:
XXX <- read.delim("Name_XXX.txt", skip=6, sep="\t", dec=".")
Remove the first two columns: Name_XXX_II <- XXX[,-1:-2].
Define a normalization function: normalize <- function(x){ x / max(x, na.rm=TRUE) }
Apply to each data column (adjust column count to the number of conditions, e.g., 1:16):
Normalized <- as.data.frame(lapply(Name_XXX_II[1:16], normalize)) * 100
Write the normalized matrix to an Excel file:
write.xlsx(Normalized, "X:/.../Name_XXX_Normalized.xlsx")
Repeat for each biological replicate and for both green and red channel files.
If decimal separator issues arise, change ‘dec’ argument or replace ‘.’ with ‘,’ before running.

steps.title: Plot normalized data in GraphPad Prism
steps.instruction: Import normalized Excel files into GraphPad Prism for visualization and statistical analysis.

substeps.instruction: Open GraphPad Prism (v10.04.0 or later).
Create a new XY data table (File → New → XY).
In ‘Data table’, choose ‘Enter or import data in new table’.
Set X‑axis to ‘Numbers’ (time points) and Y‑axis to ‘Enter number of replicate values in side‑by‑side sub‑columns’.
Define columns as ‘Mean, SD, N’.
Copy the time points into the X column and paste each condition’s normalized values into separate Y columns (one column per condition).
If needed, adjust grouping (e.g., ‘Plate Map Replicates’) to reflect technical replicates.
Create graphs, apply appropriate legends, and perform statistical tests.
If 100 % cell death is reached before 72 h, manually set later time points to 100 % to avoid underestimation of AUC.
